issues.legal_issue: A court-ordered stay of dispossession is excluded when calculating the time allowed to make an award in land-acquisition proceedings, even if the court did not stay the making of the award.
material_facts: The landowner challenged the acquisition notification in court, and the court stayed dispossession from the land.

A declaration for acquisition was subsequently published, and the award was made more than two years after that declaration, but the time during which the dispossession stay operated was excluded from the calculation.
issues.conclusion: The period during which dispossession was stayed had to be excluded from the time allowed for making the award. The acquisition proceedings therefore did not lapse, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, requires an award within two years of publication of the declaration, failing which acquisition proceedings lapse; its Explanation excludes periods during which a court stays any action or proceeding to be taken in pursuance of the declaration. The phrase is broad enough to include taking possession, whether before or after the award, and a stay of dispossession therefore counts even without a stay on making the award. The Court relied on Yusufbhai Noormohmed Nendoliya v. State of Gujarat, Sangappa Gurulingappa Sajjan v. State of Karnataka, and Government of Tamil Nadu v. Vasantha Bai.

predicates.land_acquisition_lapse_claim: A person in land-acquisition proceedings sought a ruling that the proceedings had lapsed because the award was not made within the ordinary time limit.
predicates.award_was_late_without_stay_exclusion: The award was made after the ordinary time limit when the period of a court-ordered stay is not excluded.
predicates.court_stayed_land_dispossession: A court ordered that the landowner could not be dispossessed from the land during a period relevant to the acquisition proceedings.

issues.definition: When a person claims that land-acquisition proceedings lapsed because an award was late, a court-ordered stay of dispossession means the proceedings do not lapse on account of the period covered by that stay.
